body_markdown:
In a world of[six-figure luxury pickups](https://www.hagerty.com/media/opinion/auto-anthro-why-luxury-trucks-dont-have-luxury-badges/) and restomod trucks with eye-watering build sheets, there’s something to be said for an honest truck that strikes a delicate balance between tool and toy. Not until maybe the mid-1990s were pickups considered anything other than utilitarian. For several decades prior, if you were to ask a pickup product planner, “Why isn’t this fancier?” they’d have looked at you like you’d kicked their pet.


*Who would be foolish enough to do that?*


Hagerty Marketplace | CraigZimmerman


Hagerty Marketplace | CraigZimmerman


For most of the 1980s and the early 1990s, the first-generation Dodge Ram stayed true to the honest truck ethos. Hard-working and utilitarian—perfectly emblematic of those who probably owned one. Call it whatever you want—nostalgia or truck tech fatigue—but we can’t help but hold a soft spot for these[simpler machines](https://www.hagerty.com/media/market-trends/5-collector-trucks-you-can-drive-daily-for-15k/) .


Hagerty Marketplace | CraigZimmerman


That’s probably why this[1990 Dodge Power Ram W150 4×4](https://www.hagerty.com/marketplace/auction/1990-Dodge-W150/78fd3a8b-faf3-4987-8ff4-0be7aff9d221) , currently listed on Hagerty Marketplace, immediately caught our attention. Astute observers will notice a bit of cardboard beneath the engine in these photos; the listing notes an oil leak, and while that means a little work on the back end, it doesn’t take away much from what otherwise appears to be a solid example of the end of an era.


Hagerty Marketplace | CraigZimmerman


Hagerty Marketplace | CraigZimmerman


This truck is from the closing years of the first-generation Ram, which was built on the[D/W series platform](https://www.hagerty.com/media/market-trends/hagerty-insider/even-the-most-challenging-projects-dont-tarnish-the-appeal-of-dodges-w150/) from 1981–93. The big update for the 1990 model year was the introduction of fuel injection, and this example’s 5.2-liter V-8 offers that tech. Here, that eight-pot is paired with a four-speed automatic transmission that mates to a dual-range transfer case for true 4×4 capability.


Hagerty Marketplace | CraigZimmerman


At some point in the truck’s life, it was refinished in the gray color you see here. The red tailgate letters pop nicely against that muted hue. The modification list is short and sweet: Besides the re-spray, this one wears new 15-inch alloy wheels, LED headlights, a receiver hitch, and 33-inch off-road tires.


Hagerty Marketplace | CraigZimmerman


That single-cab, long-bed configuration will always be a perfect silhouette to us. Inside, you’ll find a tan vinyl bench seat (as God intended), a massive transfer case lever, a color-matched dashboard, an AM/FM stereo, and precious little else. Again: Utility first.


Hagerty Marketplace | CraigZimmerman


Hagerty Marketplace | CraigZimmerman


Listed imperfections include the previously mentioned oil leak, some wear in the interior, a little corrosion on the underbody components, and some exterior blemishes—notably, there appears to be some sun fading on the roof. In our eyes, those are almost prerequisites for this truck to have a second life as a friendly farm truck or a weekend joyrider. Either way, this W150 Power Ram’s charm is undeniable.
